questions.problem: Write $\frac{12{x}^{3}}{4{x}^{2}+5}$ in the form $ax+\frac{bx}{4{x}^{2}+5},$ where $a\ne 0.$ What is the value of $a+b?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we factor the numerator to put $4{x}^{2}$ in parentheses. Then, we add and subtract $5$ in the parentheses. This reveals a copy of the denominator without changing the value of the expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12{x}^{3}}{4{x}^{2}+5} & =\frac{3x(4{x}^{2})}{4{x}^{2}+5} \\  & =\frac{3x(4{x}^{2}+5-5)}{4{x}^{2}+5} \\  & =\frac{3x(4{x}^{2}+5)+3x(-5)}{4{x}^{2}+5} \\  & =\frac{3x(4{x}^{2}+5)-15x}{4{x}^{2}+5}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we split the fraction into two, and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x(4{x}^{2}+5)-15x}{4{x}^{2}+5} & =\frac{3x(4{x}^{2}+5)}{4{x}^{2}+5}+\frac{-15x}{4{x}^{2}+5} \\  & =3x+\frac{-15x}{4{x}^{2}+5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have $a=3$ and $b=-15,$ and we get

$$
a+b=3+(-15)=-12.
$$

questions.problem: Write $\frac{4x-1}{4x-7}$ in the form $a+\frac{b}{4x-7},$ where $a\ne 0.$ What is the value of $a+b?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we subtract and add $7$ in the numerator. This reveals a copy of the denominator without changing the value of the expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x-1}{4x-7}=\frac{4x-7+7-1}{4x-7}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we split the fraction into two, and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4x-7+7-1}{4x-7} & =\frac{4x-7}{4x-7}+\frac{7-1}{4x-7} \\  & =1+\frac{6}{4x-7}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have $a=1$ and $b=6,$ and we get

$$
a+b=1+6=7.
$$

Write $\frac{3{x}^{6}+8}{3{x}^{6}+2x}$ in the form $a+\frac{bx+c}{3{x}^{6}+2x},$ where $a\ne 0.$
$3{x}^{6}+8$ $=$ {{field-1}} $+$ {{field-2}}
$3{x}^{6}+2x$ $3{x}^{6}+2x$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we add and subtract $2x$ in the numerator. This reveals a copy of the denominator without changing the value of the expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{6}+8}{3{x}^{6}+2x}\,=\,\frac{3{x}^{6}+2x-2x+8}{3{x}^{6}+2x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we split the fraction into two, and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{6}+2x-2x+8}{3{x}^{6}+2x} & =\frac{3{x}^{6}+2x}{3{x}^{4}+2x}+\frac{-2x+8}{3{x}^{6}+2x} \\  & =1+\frac{-2x+8}{3{x}^{6}+2x}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Write $\frac{12{x}^{7}}{6{x}^{7}+4}$ in the form $a+\frac{b}{6{x}^{7}+4},$ where $a\ne 0.$
$12{x}^{7}$ $=$ {{field-1}} $+$ {{field-2}}
$6{x}^{7}+4$ $6{x}^{7}+4$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we factor the numerator to put $6{x}^{7}$ in parentheses. Then, we add and subtract $4$ in the parentheses. This reveals a copy of the denominator without changing the value of the expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12{x}^{7}}{6{x}^{7}+4} & =\frac{2(6{x}^{7})}{6{x}^{7}+4} \\  & =\frac{2(6{x}^{7}+4-4)}{6{x}^{7}+4} \\  & =\frac{2[(6{x}^{7}+4)-(4)]}{6{x}^{7}+4} \\  & =\frac{2(6{x}^{7}+4)-2(4)}{6{x}^{7}+4} \\  & =\frac{2(6{x}^{7}+4)-8}{6{x}^{7}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we split the fraction into two, and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2(6{x}^{7}+4)-8}{6{x}^{7}+4} & =\frac{2(6{x}^{7}+4)}{6{x}^{7}+4}+\frac{-8}{6{x}^{7}+4} \\  & =2+\frac{-8}{6{x}^{7}+4}\end{aligned}
$$
